sections.h2: Which Winton offices value and bill property in Hertford County?
sections.html:
Two neighboring offices on Justice Drive in Winton split the work, and both stay open on weekdays until five in the afternoon.

Hertford County tax offices as listed on county web pages
OfficeAddressPhone
Tax Assessor115 Justice Drive, Suite 4, Winton252-358-7810
Tax Collector115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, Winton252-358-7815

The assessor's stated mission is to find, identify and appraise every taxable parcel and personal property account. The collector bills for the county and also for the towns of Ahoskie, Harrellsville, Cofield, Como, Murfreesboro and Winton, plus two drainage districts, three fire districts and solid waste fees. So one parcel's bill may carry several lines.

sections.h2: What is the Hertford County payment calendar?
sections.html:
Bills fall due on September 1. A 2 percent charge starts on January 6, and a further 3/4 of 1 percent builds for every month after that.

The postal postmark decides whether a mailed payment is late; a meter date does not count. Partial payments are welcome from the day the bill arrives until January 6. An escrow account does not stop the bill from coming to you, because the lender is told electronically and chooses which bills to pay. Call your lender if you expect it to pay.

  • Options: online, at the Winton counter, or on the toll-free line at 1-888-520-8728.
  • An online card payment adds 2.5 percent, a fee set by the processor and not kept by the county.
  • Cards are also taken at the counter.
  • A bounced check draws the G.S. 105-357(2) charge: $25.00 or 10 percent of the check, whichever is more, capped at $1,000.

sections.h2: What does the 2027 Hertford County revaluation change?
sections.html:
New real estate values take effect January 1, 2027. The last revaluation in the county was in 2019, and the state requires reappraisal at least every eight years.

Appraisers divide the county into market areas, which the county also calls neighborhoods, review recent sales in each one, and apply a uniform schedule of values so similar houses are judged by the same standard. The county hired an outside appraisal firm from North Carolina and Virginia for the 2027 cycle. Field measuring began in July 2025 to fix listing errors and capture changes since the last cycle. Owners get a notice of assessed value shortly after the effective date, and appeal instructions will appear on that notice. The old value can be compared using the parcel's 2018 tax card, which the tax office can pull.

The county says the aim is fairness among owners, and values will not all move together. Rates come from the commissioners and the town boards, typically in June. A bill is the tax value times the rate, so request the rate sheet from the tax office when you plan a sale.

sections.h2: Where do I take a disagreement over a Hertford County value?
sections.html:
Use the instructions printed on your notice of assessed value. The county says it will also post appeal forms on the Assessor's page as the revaluation date approaches.

A formal appeal is heard by the county's equalization and review board, normally the commissioners sitting in that role. In a revaluation year it wraps up by December 1, and a request to be heard has to arrive before it adjourns. Ask the assessor for the adjournment date, and see G.S. 105-322.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs apply in Hertford County?
sections.html:
North Carolina lets an owner draw on only one of its three relief programs. All are filed with the county assessor on Form AV-9. The elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker are described in G.S. 105-277.1, 105-277.1C and 105-277.1B, and the 2026 income limit printed by the Department of Revenue is $38,800.

Call the Tax Assessor at 252-358-7810 to learn which program fits and whether a filing already exists for your parcel. The state form says filings are accepted through June 1 before the tax year, and a new application is needed every year for the circuit breaker. A sale can end a deferral, so raise it before listing. Form details: NCDOR Form AV-9.

sections.h2: What if taxes are unpaid when a Hertford County house sells?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property. A lien for real property taxes attaches on the date the property must be listed, and penalties, interest and costs attach with it under G.S. 105-355. The county's FAQ adds that real property is listed in the name of the owner on January 1 each year, so a seller who conveys after that date can still receive the bill.

Practical steps for a seller:

  • Request a payoff total from the collector covering this year and any earlier years.
  • Have the closing attorney settle taxes out of proceeds, which is the wording the Register of Deeds expects on deeds.
  • Pass any bill that shows up after the sale to the new owner.

Left unpaid, a bill can lead to wage garnishment, bank attachment, attachment of state income tax refunds, levy and foreclosure. The collector's office also offers a three-month payment plan on delinquent taxes. Foreclosure auctions are held at the courthouse door, buyers pay in full with cash or certified funds, and the local newspaper carries the advertisement.

sections.h2: What vehicles, county-owned land and auctions does the collector handle?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector's pages cover more than house bills. Motor vehicles are billed within 90 days of tag renewal, owners get one month to pay before interest starts, and after four months a block goes on the tag. The county cannot prorate or reduce a vehicle bill without the FS20 receipt from NCDMV, which must reach the office within one year of surrender. The license plate agency in Ahoskie is at 907 E. Memorial Drive.

The office also lists county-owned property open for bids and foreclosed parcels with their auction dates, and it ties foreclosure sales to an outside attorney who schedules them. Properties that fail to sell at auction are sold by the county. No advance registration is needed for an auction; you or a representative simply appear at the courthouse door.

sections.h2: Who owns homes in Hertford County?
sections.html:
The county counts 8,285 households of about 2.20 people each. Ownership runs at 67.4 percent, the middle home value among owners is $119,200, and median monthly owner costs are $1,285 with a mortgage and $523 without one. Poverty affects 22.9 percent of residents, and 27.1 percent are 65 or older. These figures come from Census QuickFacts.

The county took shape in 1759 from parts of Bertie, Northampton and Chowan counties, and farming still anchors its economy. Parcels range from town lots in Ahoskie, Murfreesboro and Winton to cropland and timber, which is why the fire district and solid waste lines on a bill vary from one parcel to the next. Bring the collector's total to the closing table so nothing is left owing.

faqs.q: How can I pay my Hertford County tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay online, in person at 115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, or by calling 1-888-520-8728. Online card payments add a 2.5 percent fee, and partial payments are accepted until January 6.

faqs.q: Which office sends the Hertford County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tax Collector bills for the county, six towns, fire and drainage districts, and solid waste fees. Call 252-358-7815 with questions.

faqs.q: When does the next Hertford County revaluation take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The last one was in 2019, and owners receive notices of their new assessed values shortly after that date, with appeal instructions on the notice.

faqs.q: I sold my house but still got the Hertford County bill. Why?
faqs.a: Real property is listed in the owner's name as of January 1, so a bill can still arrive after you sell. Send a copy to the new owner, as the county asks.

faqs.q: Can I pay Hertford County taxes over time?
faqs.a: Yes for delinquent accounts: the collector offers a three-month plan. Call 252-358-7815 to ask about it.
